newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh troops fight rebels, three killed.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh troops fight rebels, three killed.

text.p: One soldier and two rebels were killed in a predawn gunbattle between the army and tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts on Saturday.
Police said the battle erupted after guerrillas captured a market at Baratali village in Bandarban hill district, and demanded troops at a nearby camp leave.
"As soldiers refused, an exchange of fire began. The shootout continued for nearly three hours with a brief break," one police officer told reporters.
Troops recovered the bodies of the soldier and guerrillas along with two Chinese-made sub-machineguns used by the rebels.
Senior officers from Chittagong army headquarters flew to the battle scene in the afternoon, accompanied by journalists.
The bodies of army Lance Naik Hamidur Rahman and the two rebels in their olive combat uniform were still lying in pools of blood outside the army camp.
Local residents including Thanchi Union Council Chairman Nurul Islam said at least 30 guerrillas surrounded the camp manned by 10 soldeirs and enganged in a fierce shootout.
"We got up from sleep and felt that bullets were flying in hundreds," Islam told reporters.
Police also recovered Bangladeshi and Indian currencies, and several documents from the dead guerrillas. A second soldier was wounded in the battle.
Government officials said Saturday's battle might put in doubt peace talks with the Shanti Bahini due on May 11.
"Definitely this will have an adverse impact on the peace efforts," one official told Reuters.

The Shantis, made up of mostly Chakma tribesmen, have forged an insurgency since 1973 after Bangladesh's rejected their demand for granting autonomy to the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which also forced some 50,000 tribespeople to flee into India.
Over 6,700 tribespeople returned home recently following an agreement between Bangladesh and India, and the next phase of repatriation was due to begin soon.
The government and rebel leaders have held two rounds of peace talks since January but made little progress.
Lieutenant-Colonel M.M. Iqbal Alam, Thanchi's local army commander, told Reuters: "If there were more such raids and ambushes by the insurgents peace won't be attained.
"If the insurgents open up firing how can we stop using our guns," said the officer in deep anguish.
Major-General Abdul Matin, General Officer Commanding of army's 24th Infantry Division, told reporters that "a section of the Shanti Bahini" was trying to foil the peace initiatives.
"They just don't want peace. They want the insurgency to continue," he said.
"The hills in Bandarban (one of three Hill Tracts districts) are the most inaccessible. The hard-core rebels may have made it their latest hideout," General Matin said.

"The uniform (of the two dead rebels), receipt books for colecting tolls and Indian and Bangladesh currency recovered from them are good enough proof that they were members of the Shanti Bahini," said Brigadier Mohammad Selim.
There are over 12,000 army soldiers and 18,000 other security forces now pitted against an estimated 2,500 guerrillas operating in the Hill Tracts, security sources said.

But the Shantis started losing nerves after Dhaka and New Delhi recently agreed to join hands in fighting insurgents along their borders and not to give shelter to cross-border "terrorists," they said.
